five_minute_explanation: One participant is the Game Master and presents the world, opposition, and consequences.
Each other participant controls a Wild Card hero.
Say what the hero attempts in ordinary language; roll only when uncertainty and consequences matter.
Traits are dice such as d4, d6, d8, d10, and d12.
A Wild Card rolls the Trait die and a d6 Wild Die, Aces maximum results, and keeps the better total.
Most unopposed Trait rolls succeed on 4; every full four above the required total is a raise.
Bennies let heroes reroll, Soak Wounds, recover from Shaken, influence initiative, or use other allowed options.
Action Cards determine turn order in rounds.
Combat compares attacks with Parry or a ranged Target Number, then compares damage with Toughness.

End with a choice or short Dramatic Task.

document.purpose: A system-neutral, beginner-friendly, copyright-safe guide to learning, playing, and running the latest edition of Savage Worlds.

Support, Tests, powers, advancement, and common subsystems

what_savage_worlds_is.summary: Savage Worlds is a genre-flexible tabletop roleplaying system designed for fast resolution, cinematic action, tactical play, and low Game Master bookkeeping.
core_design_features: Attributes and skills are rated by die type rather than a numeric bonus.
Most ordinary Trait rolls use a Target Number of 4.
Important characters are Wild Cards and roll an extra d6 Wild Die.
Dice can Ace, meaning their maximum result is rerolled and added.
Every 4 points above the required total is a raise.
Players spend Bennies to reroll, Soak Wounds, alter initiative, and influence play.
Initiative normally uses a standard deck of playing cards with two Jokers.
Named heroes and major villains take multiple Wounds; most Extras are removed by one Wound.
Setting Rules deliberately tune the core engine for different genres and tones.

required.details: Savage Worlds Adventure Edition, preferably the version 5.0 PDF or fifth-printing book.
A standard 54-card deck: 52 playing cards plus two Jokers.
Coins, poker chips, stones, or other visible tokens.
The official SWADE sheet or a compatible digital sheet.
One person runs the world and rules; the other participants portray player characters.

optional: The free official Test Drive adventure
not_required: The Savage Worlds Essentials boxed set

players: Speak and make decisions for their characters.
Roll Traits when the outcome is uncertain and meaningful.
Track Bennies, Wounds, Fatigue, gear, powers, and temporary conditions.
Help establish character goals, relationships, and genre tone.
Respect the agreed safety tools and table boundaries.
game_master: Presents situations, locations, nonplayer characters, dangers, and consequences.
Decides when a roll is required and selects the relevant Trait.
Runs Extras, villains, hazards, and the Action Deck.
Awards Bennies for entertaining, thematic, clever, or heroic play.
Applies the core rules, setting rules, and current errata consistently.
Makes prompt rulings when an obscure question would otherwise stop play.
shared_responsibilities: Agree on the setting, campaign premise, tone, and allowable content.
Know which Setting Rules and optional subsystems are active.
Keep descriptions connected to the fiction rather than treating rolls as isolated buttons.
Correct honest rules mistakes without turning the session into an argument.

core_vocabulary.Trait: An Attribute or Skill represented by a die type.
core_vocabulary.Attribute: One of Agility, Smarts, Spirit, Strength, or Vigor.
core_vocabulary.Skill: A learned capability such as Athletics, Fighting, Notice, Persuasion, Shooting, or Stealth.
core_vocabulary.Target_Number: The total required for success. The usual unopposed Target Number is 4.
core_vocabulary.Raise: Each full 4 points by which a successful result exceeds the required total.
core_vocabulary.Ace: When a die rolls its maximum value, roll it again and add; it may Ace repeatedly.
core_vocabulary.Wild_Card: A major character who rolls a Wild Die, has Bennies, and can normally suffer three Wounds.
core_vocabulary.Extra: A supporting character who normally rolls no Wild Die and is Incapacitated by one Wound.
core_vocabulary.Wild_Die: An extra d6 rolled with a Wild Card's Trait die; use the better result.
core_vocabulary.Benny: A spendable token that gives a player or the Game Master limited control over luck and survival.
core_vocabulary.Action_Card: A playing card that determines turn order in rounds.
core_vocabulary.Shaken: A temporary rattled state that restricts actions until the character recovers.
core_vocabulary.Wound: Serious harm that applies a cumulative penalty and can lead to Incapacitation.
core_vocabulary.Fatigue: A separate track for exhaustion, exposure, and similar non-Wound harm.
core_vocabulary.Edge: A beneficial character ability with requirements.
core_vocabulary.Hindrance: A meaningful complication, flaw, obligation, or disadvantage.
core_vocabulary.Advance: A character improvement earned during a campaign.
core_vocabulary.Rank: A broad experience tier: Novice, Seasoned, Veteran, Heroic, or Legendary.
core_vocabulary.Setting_Rule: A campaign-level rule that changes how the core engine behaves.

procedure: State what the character is trying to accomplish and how.
The Game Master decides whether a roll is necessary.
The Game Master selects the relevant Attribute or Skill and identifies modifiers or opposition.
Roll the Trait die.
If the character is a Wild Card, also roll a d6 Wild Die and use the better total.
Ace any die that rolls its maximum value by rerolling and adding.
Apply all modifiers to the chosen result.
Compare the total with the Target Number or opposing total.
Determine success, raises, failure, or Critical Failure.
Narrate the result and apply consequences.

raises.rule: Every full 4 points above the required total is one raise.

wild_die.rule: A Wild Card rolls the relevant Trait die and a d6 Wild Die, then uses the higher result. The dice are not added together.
wild_die.modifiers: Apply modifiers after selecting the better die total.
wild_die.multiple_actions: A Wild Card receives a Wild Die for each action, not one Wild Die for every individual attack die generated by Rate of Fire or another special rule.

acing.rule: Trait and damage dice are open-ended. When a die rolls its highest face, roll it again and add the new result. Repeat while maximum results continue.

critical_failure.wild_card: A natural 1 on both the Trait die and Wild Die is a Critical Failure. It automatically fails, may create an additional complication, and cannot be rerolled with a Benny.
critical_failure.extra: When it matters whether an Extra's natural 1 is critical, the Game Master may roll a d6; on a 1 it is a Critical Failure.

unskilled_attempts.rule: Roll d4-2, plus the Wild Die for a Wild Card, unless the skill cannot reasonably be attempted untrained.
unskilled_attempts.warning: The penalty applies to the selected total after choosing between the Trait die and Wild Die.

procedure: The acting character rolls first unless the specific rule says otherwise.
The opposing character rolls the resistance Trait.
The acting character must achieve at least a basic success and beat the opposing total.
Ties normally favor the defender or the status quo.
Every full 4 points over the opposing total is a raise.

when_not_to_roll: The task is routine and there is no meaningful pressure.
Failure would not change the situation.
The character has enough time and resources that success is certain.
The roll would merely block essential information with no alternative route.
A different subsystem already resolves the situation.

probability_intuition.note: These percentages show the chance to meet an unmodified Target Number of 4. They are included to help new players understand die steps; they are not normally needed during play.
probability_intuition.lesson: A die-step increase matters, but the Wild Die and Bennies make Wild Cards much more reliable than Extras without making success automatic.

attributes.Agility: Coordination, dexterity, reflexes, and bodily control.
attributes.Smarts: Reasoning, education, perception of patterns, and mental adaptability.
attributes.Spirit: Willpower, courage, confidence, and inner resolve.
attributes.Strength: Physical power and the basis of many melee damage rolls.
attributes.Vigor: Endurance, health, resistance, Toughness, and Soak rolls.

die_scale: d12+1 and higher for exceptional cases
skill_principles: Each skill is linked to an Attribute for character-building cost.
A linked Attribute does not automatically add to the skill roll.
A setting may add, remove, rename, or restrict skills.
Arcane Backgrounds may provide specialized arcane skills.
traits.skill_list_warning: Not every campaign uses every listed skill. Use the skill list and arcane skills in the current core book and the selected setting.

character_creation.overview: SWADE character creation is point-based. A setting may change ancestry options, starting power, gear, allowed Edges, skills, and Setting Rules.

standard_steps.name: Campaign and concept
instructions: Read the campaign premise and Setting Rules.
Choose a concept that fits the party and intended tone.
Decide what the character wants, fears, protects, and contributes.

standard_steps.name: Ancestry or race
instructions: Choose an ancestry allowed by the setting.
Apply its positive and negative abilities.
In the core baseline, humans commonly receive a free Edge, but setting rules may replace this.

standard_steps.name: Attributes
instructions: Start Agility, Smarts, Spirit, Strength, and Vigor at d4.
Spend 5 Attribute points.
Each die-step increase costs 1 point.
The normal starting maximum is d12 unless the setting says otherwise.

standard_steps.name: Skills
instructions: Begin the five core skills at d4 under standard SWADE creation.
Spend 12 skill points.
A die-step costs 1 point while the skill is no higher than its linked Attribute.
A die-step above the linked Attribute costs 2 points.
Buying a non-core skill at d4 costs its first skill point.

standard_steps.name: Derived statistics
instructions: Calculate Pace, Parry, and Toughness.
Record Size and any ancestry or Edge modifications.
Add worn torso armor to Toughness as Armor.

standard_steps.name: Hindrances
instructions: Choose Hindrances that will genuinely appear in play.
A Minor Hindrance is normally worth 1 character-building point.
A Major Hindrance is normally worth 2 points.
The standard character-building benefit is capped at 4 Hindrance points.

standard_steps.name: Spend Hindrance points
standard_options: 2 points: gain one additional Attribute point.
2 points: take an Edge for which the character qualifies.
1 point: gain one additional skill point.
1 point: increase starting funds, using the current core or setting rule.

standard_steps.name: Edges
instructions: Choose any free ancestry Edge and Edges purchased with Hindrance points.
Check Rank, Trait, and prerequisite requirements.
Arcane Background Edges unlock powers and define their arcane skill and special rules.

standard_steps.name: Gear
instructions: Use the campaign's starting funds or equipment package.
Record weapon Range, Damage, Armor Penetration, Rate of Fire, Shots, Minimum Strength, and notes.
Record armor location and Armor value.
Confirm restricted, rare, or setting-inappropriate equipment with the Game Master.

standard_steps.name: Finishing details
instructions: Name the character.
Write a short background and current motivation.
Connect the character to at least one other hero or important nonplayer character.
Record languages, appearance, beliefs, obligations, and campaign hooks.
Check all totals and prerequisites.

derived_statistics.Pace: Usually 6 inches for a standard human, before modifiers.
derived_statistics.Parry: 2 + half the Fighting die. A character without Fighting normally has Parry 2.
derived_statistics.Toughness: 2 + half the Vigor die + torso Armor, before other modifiers.
derived_statistics.Running: Normally adds a d6 inches of movement and imposes the standard running penalty to other actions that turn.
derived_statistics.tabletop_scale: One tabletop inch normally represents two yards in the game world.

hindrance_advice: Choose Hindrances that create decisions, scenes, or complications rather than passive bookkeeping.
Do not use a Hindrance as permission to sabotage the group.
Ask how frequently a campaign expects a Hindrance to matter.
A Hindrance should be roleplayed even after its character-building points are spent.
The Game Master should reward meaningful complications with Bennies when appropriate.

sample_character.name: Mira Vale
sample_character.concept: Human expedition scout and field medic
edge_example: One Edge purchased with Hindrance points
sample_character.legal_build_note: This is an illustrative core-framework build. Select actual Edge and Hindrance names, gear, and any setting changes with the current core and campaign books.

advantages: Roll a d6 Wild Die with Trait rolls.
Normally begin a session with three Bennies.
Can normally suffer three Wounds before Incapacitation.

rules: Do not normally roll a Wild Die.
Are normally Incapacitated by one Wound.
Similar Extras often act on one shared Action Card.
Can still Ace, score raises, use tactics, and be dangerous.

wild_cards_and_extras.gm_guideline: Use Wild Cards for characters whose survival, identity, or dramatic importance deserves extra table time. Using too many Wild Card opponents can slow the game and weaken the distinction.

starting_pools.game_master_common_pool: One Benny per player character at the start of the session.
starting_pools.game_master_wild_card_npc: Each Game Master Wild Card normally has two personal Bennies.

bennies.carry_over: Unused Bennies normally do not carry from one session to the next.
common_ways_to_earn: Roleplaying a Hindrance in a way that creates a real complication
Making the table laugh without disrupting the tone
A Joker being dealt, when the rule grants Bennies to the players

standard_uses.details: Reroll a Trait check and keep the best result. A Critical Failure cannot be rerolled.
Remove Shaken immediately, even outside the character's turn when allowed.
Immediately after one source causes Wounds, make a Vigor roll; each success and raise removes one incoming Wound.
After Action Cards and card-affecting Edges or Hindrances are resolved, discard the current card and draw another.
Reroll the full damage roll, including a bonus damage die earned from an attack raise, and keep the better result.
A character with an Arcane Background may spend a Benny to regain 5 Power Points.
With Game Master approval, introduce a plausible clue, item, contact, or minor favorable detail. This is intentionally bounded by the campaign's tone and established facts.

bennies.good_player_habit: Spend Bennies. They are a renewable session resource, not a permanent score.
bennies.good_gm_habit: Award Bennies early enough that players feel safe using them, but attach awards to behavior the group wants to encourage.

before_play: Confirm the active core version, errata, setting book, and Setting Rules.
Review safety tools and prohibited or veiled content.
Recap the previous session and current objectives.
Refresh Bennies and other session-based resources.
Prepare the Action Deck and status markers.
scene_loop: The Game Master frames the current situation.
Players ask questions and describe actions.
The Game Master answers obvious information freely.
When uncertainty and meaningful stakes exist, call for a Trait roll or subsystem.
Resolve success, raises, failure, or a complication.
Update the fiction, position, resources, and consequences.
Move to the next meaningful decision.
when_rounds_begin: A chase, Dramatic Task, or another timed sequence needs precise order.
The Game Master decides moment-by-moment timing matters.
after_play: Resolve immediate recovery and end-of-session effects.
Note unresolved threats and character goals.
Clarify any rules question that was temporarily ruled at the table.
Gather brief feedback on pacing, tone, and desired next steps.

deal: Deal one Action Card face up to each Wild Card.
Deal a shared Action Card to each group of similar Extras.
Edges and Hindrances may alter the number or choice of cards.

countdown.rank_order: Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10 down through 2

joker: The character may act whenever desired during the round and may interrupt automatically.
The character adds +2 to Trait and damage rolls for the round.
The players receive a Benny under the standard rule.
Reshuffle the deck at the end of a round in which a Joker was dealt.
hold: A character may go On Hold instead of acting when the card is called.
A Held action can be taken later in the round.
Interrupting another action may require the opposed roll specified by the current core rules.
A Held card normally carries into the next round, so the character is not dealt a new card until it is used.
why_cards_matter: Edges can make fast or hesitant characters feel mechanically distinct.
The deck supports chases, Dramatic Tasks, and other subsystems.

normal_turn: Move up to Pace as a free action.
Take one regular action without a multi-action penalty.
Take reasonable free actions such as brief speech, dropping an item, or going prone.

multiple_actions.declaration: Declare all regular actions before rolling any dice.
multiple_actions.free_actions: Free actions are not subject to the multi-action penalty.
multiple_actions.movement: Movement may usually be split before, between, and after actions.

running.procedure: Roll the character's running die and add it to Pace.
running.cost: Running counts as an action and normally imposes -2 on the character's other actions that turn.
running.note: The running die is not a Trait roll, so it has no Wild Die and does not Ace unless a rule says otherwise.

actions_and_movement.free_action_limits: Free actions are not unlimited permission to perform complex tasks. The Game Master decides when an activity requires a regular action.

combat.combat_round: A complete countdown of Action Cards. A round represents roughly six seconds when exact time matters.

melee_attacks.success: The attack hits; roll melee damage.
melee_attacks.raise: Add one bonus d6 to the damage roll. Additional attack raises do not add more bonus dice unless a special rule says otherwise.
melee_attacks.withdrawing: Leaving close combat can allow adjacent, non-Shaken opponents an immediate free attack. Use the exact current rule for unusual movement or special abilities.

skills.Shooting: Most firearms, bows, and direct ranged weapons.
skills.Athletics: Thrown weapons and appropriate physical projectiles.

damage.ranged: Roll the weapon's listed damage dice and modifiers.
damage.melee: Roll Strength plus the weapon's damage die or dice, subject to Minimum Strength and weapon rules.
damage.wild_die: Damage is not a Trait roll and does not receive a Wild Die.
damage.attack_raise_bonus: A successful attack with at least one raise normally adds +1d6 damage once.

armor_and_ap.Armor: Adds to Toughness when it protects the hit location.
armor_and_ap.Armor_Penetration: Ignores that many points of applicable Armor, but does not reduce innate Toughness.
armor_and_ap.heavy_damage: Some settings distinguish Heavy Weapons and Heavy Armor; follow the relevant core or setting rules.

step_by_step: Total all damage dice and modifiers, including Aces.
Apply Armor Penetration and the target's applicable Armor.
Compare damage with the target's Toughness.
Below Toughness: no game effect from that hit.
Toughness through Toughness+3: the target is Shaken.
Each full 4 points above Toughness is one Wound.
If a target was already Shaken and suffers another simple Shaken result from damage, it takes one Wound and remains Shaken.
A damage result that causes one or more Wounds also leaves the target Shaken.

effects: The character may take free actions but cannot take normal actions until recovered.
At the start of the character's turn, make a Spirit roll as a free action.
On success, remove Shaken and act normally.
A Benny can remove Shaken immediately.
shaken.important_distinction: Shaken is not itself a Wound.

wounds.extras: An Extra is normally Incapacitated by one Wound.
wounds.wild_cards: A Wild Card can normally suffer three Wounds and is Incapacitated when another Wound would be taken.
wounds.penalty: Each Wound gives a cumulative -1 to Pace and Trait rolls, normally to a maximum of -3.
wounds.damage_source: Resolve all Wounds from a single damage roll together before deciding whether to Soak.

soak_rolls.timing: Immediately after determining Wounds from one source, before applying them.
soak_rolls.roll: Vigor, including the Wild Die for a Wild Card.
soak_rolls.result: Each success and raise removes one Wound from that damage event.
soak_rolls.shaken: If all incoming Wounds are Soaked, the character also removes Shaken from that attack.
soak_rolls.rerolls: Additional Bennies may reroll the Soak attempt under the current reroll rules.

example.outcome: Success plus one raise removes both incoming Wounds.

incapacitation.summary: When a Wild Card is Incapacitated, make the required Vigor roll and use the current Incapacitation rules. Possible results include immediate death, Bleeding Out, stabilization, unconsciousness, and an Injury.
incapacitation.bleeding_out: A Bleeding Out character makes repeated Vigor rolls until stabilized, healed, or dead, as specified by the current core rules.
incapacitation.why_core_book_is_needed: The exact Injury, Bleeding Out, and recovery procedures are table-sensitive and should be read from the current version 5.0 rules.

fatigue.recovery: Recovery time depends on the source, such as heat, cold, hunger, sleep loss, or a power.

common_tactical_options.purpose: Improve an ally's Trait roll.
Make an enemy Distracted or Vulnerable and possibly Shaken.
Trade defense for a stronger melee attack.
Increase Parry at the cost of offensive activity.
Improve a later ranged attack or offset selected penalties.
Target a specific location for a special effect at a penalty.
Restrain, crush, or control a target.
Move or knock down an opponent.
Gain an advantage when several allies threaten one defender.
Change defense and movement interactions.

combat.tactical_option_warning: Exact bonuses, limits, and interactions for combat options should be taken from the current Combat Options chapter or official quick-reference chart.

support.purpose: One character helps another perform a Trait roll.
procedure: Describe a distinct, plausible way to help.
Roll a relevant supporting skill.
A success normally grants +1 to the supported roll.
A raise normally grants +2.
Multiple helpers are normally capped at a total +4.
A Critical Failure normally imposes -2 instead.
The support bonus must be used within the timing allowed by the rule.
restrictions: The helper's action must be meaningfully different or useful.
The Game Master may limit repetitive use of the same method.
Support does not replace the lead character's required roll.

tests.purpose: Use wit, intimidation, trickery, terrain, or another creative skill to hinder an opponent.
procedure: Describe the tactic and choose an appropriate skill.
The target resists with the Attribute linked to that skill or the resistance specified by the rule.
On success, choose to make the target Distracted or Vulnerable.
On a raise, the target is also Shaken.
The description must fit the selected skill and situation.

conditions.Distracted: -2 to the affected character's Trait rolls until the condition ends.
conditions.Vulnerable: Actions and attacks against the affected character gain +2 until the condition ends.

creative_examples: Use Athletics to kick debris into a foe's face.
Use Intimidation to make a guard hesitate.
Use Repair to vent steam from a machine beside an enemy.
Use Performance to create a disorienting distraction.

immediate_first_aid: The Healing skill can treat recent Wounds during the Golden Hour.
A successful treatment generally removes one Wound; a raise generally removes two.
Apply the patient's Wound penalties to the healer's roll as required by the current rule.
A healer normally gets one attempt per patient for a given set of Wounds.
natural_healing: Wild Cards periodically make Vigor rolls to recover Wounds.
Recovery frequency and modifiers depend on the current core rules, medical care, environment, and setting.
Extras are normally either removed from play or handled narratively unless their recovery matters.
healing_and_recovery.powers: Healing powers use their own Range, Power Point, timing, and modifier rules.
healing_and_recovery.injuries: Temporary or permanent Injuries can result from Incapacitation and may require extended or special healing.

powers_and_arcane_backgrounds.overview: Savage Worlds models magic, miracles, psionics, super-science, gifts, and similar abilities through Arcane Backgrounds, powers, Power Points, arcane skills, trappings, and Power Modifiers.
arcane_background_defines: Any setting-specific duties, components, or consequences
activation_sequence: Choose a known power.
Describe its trapping and target.
Choose legal Power Modifiers.
Calculate the final Power Point cost.
Spend or commit the required Power Points.
Roll the appropriate arcane skill.
On failure, the power does not activate and the caster normally loses 1 Power Point.
On a Critical Failure, apply the Arcane Background's backlash and end the action or turn as specified.
On success, resolve the power.
A raise often improves the listed effect.

power_points.default_recovery: Five spent Power Points per hour unless an Edge, setting, or special rule changes this.
power_points.benny_option: Spend a Benny to regain 5 Power Points.
power_points.maintenance: Some powers can be maintained or extended by paying the listed ongoing cost.

trappings.definition: The narrative appearance, method, energy, material, religion, technology, or theme of a power.
examples: A bolt may be fire, ice, lightning, spectral arrows, insects, or telekinetic force.
Protection may be armor, a force field, divine light, or hardened skin.
Healing may be prayer, nanotechnology, psychic repair, or alchemy.
trappings.rule: A trapping does not automatically grant extra mechanical benefits. The Game Master decides when the fiction creates a logical interaction.

powers_and_arcane_backgrounds.power_modifiers: Power Modifiers spend additional Power Points or alter a power at the moment of activation. Use the exact modifier list attached to that power in the current rules.
powers_and_arcane_backgrounds.setting_warning: Power availability, rank, cost, Range, Duration, trappings, backlash, and modifiers may change substantially in a Savage Setting or Companion.

advancement.advance_meaning: An Advance is one package of character improvement awarded by the campaign.
standard_advance_options: Gain a new Edge for which the character qualifies.
Increase one skill that is equal to or higher than its linked Attribute by one die type.
Increase two skills that are lower than their linked Attributes by one die type each.
Buy a new skill at d4.
Increase one Attribute by one die type, normally no more than once per Rank before Legendary.
Use any additional improvement option explicitly allowed by the current core or setting rules.

worked_examples.name: Basic Wild Card Trait roll
worked_examples.situation: A hero with Notice d8 searches a dark office.
worked_examples.calculation: Use the Wild Die result 6, then apply -2 for a total of 4.

worked_examples.name: Acing
worked_examples.situation: A hero rolls Shooting d6.
worked_examples.calculation: The d6 Aces on 6, so roll again and add: 6+4=10.
worked_examples.result: Against Target Number 4, this is a success with one raise.

worked_examples.name: Opposed roll
worked_examples.situation: A hero tries to bluff a guard.
worked_examples.result: The hero succeeds but does not earn a raise because the margin is only 2.

worked_examples.name: Support
worked_examples.situation: One hero maps a tunnel while another checks structural clues.
worked_examples.result: The supporting roll succeeds with a raise and grants +2 to the lead roll.

worked_examples.name: Test
worked_examples.situation: A hero uses Taunt to provoke a mercenary.
worked_examples.result: Success with a raise: choose Distracted or Vulnerable, and the mercenary is also Shaken.

worked_examples.name: Melee attack and damage
worked_examples.situation: A hero attacks a foe with Parry 5.
worked_examples.note: Only one bonus d6 is added for the attack raise unless another rule says otherwise.

worked_examples.name: Damage result
worked_examples.situation: A target has Toughness 6 and takes 14 damage.
worked_examples.calculation: 14 is 8 over Toughness, which is two raises.

worked_examples.name: Soak
worked_examples.situation: A Wild Card would take two Wounds and spends a Benny.
worked_examples.calculation: A success plus one raise removes two incoming Wounds.
worked_examples.result: Both Wounds are Soaked and the attack's Shaken result is removed.

worked_examples.name: Two actions
worked_examples.situation: A hero wants to Test one enemy and shoot another.
worked_examples.result: Declare both actions first; apply -2 to the Test and the Shooting roll.

worked_examples.name: Power activation
worked_examples.situation: A caster activates a power and adds a legal modifier.
procedure: Add the modifier's Power Point cost.
Spend the final cost.
Roll the Arcane Skill.
Resolve success or raise using the power entry.

quick_reference.trait_roll: Trait die + d6 Wild Die for a Wild Card; keep the better result; usual TN 4.
quick_reference.ace: Maximum die result: reroll and add, repeating as needed.
quick_reference.raise: Every full +4 over the required total.
quick_reference.critical_failure: Natural 1 on both Trait and Wild Die; cannot be rerolled.
quick_reference.unskilled: d4-2, plus Wild Die if a Wild Card.
quick_reference.multi_action: Up to three actions; two actions are -2 to all, three are -4 to all.
quick_reference.initiative: Action Cards, Ace high; ties: Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs.
quick_reference.joker: Act anytime, +2 to Trait and damage rolls for the round, players gain a Benny, reshuffle afterward.
quick_reference.ranged: Usually TN 4, modified by Range, cover, illumination, and circumstances.
quick_reference.shaken: Damage from Toughness to Toughness+3, or another simple Shaken result while already Shaken causes a Wound.
quick_reference.wounds: Each full +4 damage over Toughness is one Wound.
quick_reference.extra_wounds: Normally one Wound Incapacitates an Extra.
quick_reference.soak: Spend a Benny; Vigor roll; each success and raise removes one incoming Wound.
quick_reference.test: Opposed creative skill use; success causes Distracted or Vulnerable; raise also Shaken.
quick_reference.power_points: Default recovery is 5 per hour; a Benny can restore 5.

common_mistakes.mistake: Adding the Trait die and Wild Die together.
common_mistakes.correction: Roll both and use the higher result.

common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting that both dice can Ace.
common_mistakes.correction: Ace the Trait die and Wild Die independently, then choose the better final total.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating every 4 over Toughness as only Shaken.
common_mistakes.correction: Each full 4 over Toughness causes a Wound.

State obvious stakes before the roll.
Let a raise matter.
Use Extras for speed and Wild Cards for dramatic focus.
Award Bennies regularly enough that players use them.
Use conditions, Tests, cover, and terrain instead of only increasing enemy Toughness.
Choose the subsystem that matches the scene's dramatic purpose.
Make a temporary ruling, continue play, and verify obscure details later.
Apply current errata rather than mixing printings accidentally.

difficulty_guidance.challenging: Apply -2 when circumstances are distinctly difficult.
difficulty_guidance.very_difficult: Apply -4 only when the obstacle is exceptional.
difficulty_guidance.extreme: Use larger penalties rarely and ensure the group understands the risk.
difficulty_guidance.opposed: Use an opposed roll when another active character is directly resisting.

encounter_design: Give the opposition an objective other than simply reducing every hero to zero.
Mix melee, ranged, mobile, and support threats.
Create terrain that invites movement and Tests.
Use waves or reinforcements instead of placing every Extra at once.
Include surrender, retreat, negotiation, rescue, or environmental solutions.
Remember that exploding damage dice make every attack potentially dangerous.
Avoid overloading encounters with high-Toughness Wild Cards.
running_extras_fast: Group identical Extras on a shared Action Card.
Use one visual marker per status.
Remove Incapacitated Extras promptly unless their fate matters.
Use average tactics and clear objectives.
Roll groups together only when the current rule allows it.
Do not give every minor enemy a custom Edge list.
benny_economy: Begin with the correct Game Master pool.
Spend villain Bennies to preserve important scenes, not every disposable Extra.
Award player Bennies for the behaviors named during session zero.
Place physical Bennies where everyone can see the current economy.
Do not revoke earned Bennies as punishment.
failure_design: Failure can cost time.
Failure can consume ammunition, Power Points, money, or favors.
Failure can worsen position.
Failure can reveal the heroes.
Failure can create a difficult choice.
Failure can provide incomplete or dangerous information.
Failure should not automatically halt the campaign when another consequence is more interesting.

common_mistakes.mistake: Adding the Trait die and Wild Die together.
common_mistakes.correction: Roll both and use the higher result.

common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting that both dice can Ace.
common_mistakes.correction: Ace the Trait die and Wild Die independently, then choose the better final total.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating every 4 over Toughness as only Shaken.
common_mistakes.correction: Each full 4 over Toughness causes a Wound.

common_mistakes.mistake: Adding multiple bonus d6s for several raises on an attack roll.
common_mistakes.correction: The standard attack raise adds one bonus d6 damage once.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using the Wild Die on damage.
common_mistakes.correction: Damage is not a Trait roll.

common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting Wound penalties on Soak or other Trait rolls.
common_mistakes.correction: Apply current Wound penalties unless an Edge or rule ignores them.

common_mistakes.mistake: Waiting too long to spend Bennies.
common_mistakes.correction: Bennies normally reset each session.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using only attacks in combat.
common_mistakes.correction: Support, Tests, Hold, cover, movement, grapples, and objectives are core tools.

common_mistakes.mistake: Mixing SWD and SWADE rules.
common_mistakes.correction: Check the product abbreviation, current core version, and conversion notes.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming a rule from Deadlands, Pathfinder for Savage Worlds, Rifts, or a Companion is universal.
common_mistakes.correction: Separate core rules, Setting Rules, and setting-specific abilities.

common_mistakes.mistake: Calling for rolls when failure has no consequence.
common_mistakes.correction: Move the fiction forward without rolling.

common_mistakes.mistake: Making every significant enemy a Wild Card.
common_mistakes.correction: Reserve Wild Cards for major dramatic figures.

common_mistakes.mistake: Treating concise catalog summaries as complete rules text.
common_mistakes.correction: Use catalog entries for discovery and data entry; use the current licensed book for exact requirements and effects.

common_mistakes.mistake: Applying a Companion or Savage Setting option as universal core.
common_mistakes.correction: Every imported option needs a source and scope field.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using tabletop movement, chase position, and real-world speed interchangeably.
common_mistakes.correction: Record which scale and subsystem is active.

common_mistakes.mistake: Giving every NPC a full player-character build.
common_mistakes.correction: Assign only statistics and abilities that matter to the NPC's role.

quick_reference.trait_roll: Trait die + d6 Wild Die for a Wild Card; keep the better result; usual TN 4.
quick_reference.ace: Maximum die result: reroll and add, repeating as needed.
quick_reference.raise: Every full +4 over the required total.
quick_reference.critical_failure: Natural 1 on both Trait and Wild Die; cannot be rerolled.
quick_reference.unskilled: d4-2, plus Wild Die if a Wild Card.
quick_reference.multi_action: Up to three actions; two actions are -2 to all, three are -4 to all.
quick_reference.initiative: Action Cards, Ace high; ties: Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs.
quick_reference.joker: Act anytime, +2 to Trait and damage rolls for the round, players gain a Benny, reshuffle afterward.
quick_reference.ranged: Usually TN 4, modified by Range, cover, illumination, and circumstances.
quick_reference.shaken: Damage from Toughness to Toughness+3, or another simple Shaken result while already Shaken causes a Wound.
quick_reference.wounds: Each full +4 damage over Toughness is one Wound.
quick_reference.extra_wounds: Normally one Wound Incapacitates an Extra.
quick_reference.soak: Spend a Benny; Vigor roll; each success and raise removes one incoming Wound.
quick_reference.test: Opposed creative skill use; success causes Distracted or Vulnerable; raise also Shaken.
quick_reference.power_points: Default recovery is 5 per hour; a Benny can restore 5.
quick_reference.ranks: Novice 0-3, Seasoned 4-7, Veteran 8-11, Heroic 12-15, Legendary 16+ Advances.

compatibility_and_conversion.swade_material: Material marked SWADE is designed for the current Adventure Edition framework.
compatibility_and_conversion.swd_material: Older Savage Worlds Deluxe material is often broadly convertible, but skill names, Charisma, Shaken rules, chase rules, powers, Edges, and other details may differ.
conversion_best_practice: Use an official conversion document when available.
Replace obsolete skills with their SWADE equivalents.
Use current versions of Edges, Hindrances, powers, and special abilities.
Ignore older Charisma statistics unless the conversion says otherwise.
Use current core combat, condition, chase, and power procedures.
Do not combine two editions' versions of the same rule.

catalog_policy.scope: Setting-neutral SWADE core identities and structural summaries.
catalog_policy.exact_rules_policy: Exact proprietary rules text and complete numeric prerequisites are not reproduced.
catalog_policy.verification_rule: Validate every chosen Edge, Hindrance, power, ancestry ability, and Setting Rule against the current licensed source.
catalog_policy.companion_content: Companion-only and Savage Setting options must be stored in separate source-scoped catalogs.

validation_rules.test: Total starting Attribute die-step increases from d4 must equal or not exceed the allowed Attribute budget after ancestry and Hindrance purchases.
Skill costs must account for the linked Attribute breakpoint: each step at or below the Attribute costs one, each step above costs two.
Standard characters begin the five core skills at d4 before spending normal skill points unless a setting rule changes this.
No more than the standard cap of Hindrance points may fund starting improvements unless the setting explicitly changes it.
Every Edge must meet its Rank, Trait, ancestry, Arcane Background, and prerequisite Edge requirements.
Parry must equal 2 plus half the Fighting die, then apply modifiers.
Toughness must equal 2 plus half the Vigor die plus applicable torso Armor, Size, and modifiers.
Check Minimum Strength for armor and every carried weapon used.
Every power requires a legal Arcane Background or setting-specific source.
Rank must match Advance count: Novice 0-3, Seasoned 4-7, Veteran 8-11, Heroic 12-15, Legendary 16+.

formulas.toughness: 2 + half the Vigor die + Size + applicable torso Armor + modifiers
formulas.pace: ancestry base Pace + Edge, Hindrance, Wound, and condition modifiers
formulas.wound_penalty: negative one per current Wound, normally capped at negative three
formulas.fatigue_penalty: Fatigued negative one; Exhausted negative two
formulas.raises: floor((total - required_total) / 4) when total meets or exceeds required_total
formulas.wild_card_success: 1 - P(Trait fails) × P(Wild d6 fails), after accounting for open-ended Aces and modifiers

Raise two skills that are each below their linked Attributes by one die type.

design_workflow: Start from the NPC's fictional role and objective.
Assign only Traits likely to matter.
Add a short list of Edges or special abilities.
Give clear tactics, morale, and retreat conditions.
Mark whether the NPC is a Wild Card.
Test action economy and expected damage against the party.

advantages: Roll a d6 Wild Die with Trait rolls.
Normally begin a session with three Bennies.
Can normally suffer three Wounds before Incapacitation.

rules: Do not normally roll a Wild Die.
Are normally Incapacitated by one Wound.
Similar Extras often act on one shared Action Card.
Can still Ace, score raises, use tactics, and be dangerous.

wild_card_vs_extra.gm_guideline: Use Wild Cards for characters whose survival, identity, or dramatic importance deserves extra table time. Using too many Wild Card opponents can slow the game and weaken the distinction.

encounter_builder.balance_warning: Savage Worlds does not use a universal encounter-budget formula equivalent to a fixed challenge rating. Exploding damage, tactics, terrain, Bennies, and objectives can dominate nominal statistics.
recommended_checks: Can the heroes identify the objective?
Can both melee and ranged characters contribute?
Is there useful cover or terrain?
How do enemies react when their leader falls?
What ends the encounter besides total elimination?
How many enemy Wild Cards will slow play?

probability_reference.method: Exact recursive probability for open-ended Acing dice. Wild Card probability is one minus the product of the independent failure probabilities of the Trait die and d6 Wild Die.
assumptions: Modifiers applied after choosing the better die
interpretation: A larger Trait die primarily improves reliability and raise frequency.
The d6 Wild Die gives even d4 Wild Cards a substantial baseline chance.
A -2 modifier is significant; a -4 modifier is severe.
Benny rerolls greatly change mission-critical odds and are intentionally excluded from the base tables.
